title: Technology Sector Update for 01/04/2018: CLRO,INTC,MARK,XGTI,FFIV
text:

Technology stocks were trending higher Thursday, with shares of tech companies in the S&P 500 adding almost 0.6% in value today while the Philadelphia semiconductor index was posting a more than 0.6% gain.
In industry news:
- Intel ( INTC ) retreated again on Thursday, at one point falling almost 6%, as the chip-making giant continued to grapple with the fallout from reports its chips dating as far back as 1995 are susceptible to hacking because of a design flaw. The company also was pushing back today against accusations CEO Brian Krzanich may have cashed in before the design flaw became public by selling 3,180 of his Intel shares in November. But an Intel spokeswoman denied any wrongdoing by the executive, telling Marketwatch the Nov. 1 stock sale was part of a 10b5-1 plan adopted the previous month to systematically sell a portion of his 498,923-share stake.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
- ClearOne ( CLRO ) declined today after the audio and visual communication company said U.S. authorities have granted patent protection for its video streaming technology. The new patent covers technology enabling decoders to play back a video stream while staying synchronized with encoder, eliminating jerky, stuttering, video playback.
In other sector news:
+ F5 Networks ( FFIV ) rose after analysts at BMO Capital today raised their investment call to Outperform and also increased their price target for the company's stock by $34 to $156 a share.
- XG Technology, Inc ( XGTI ) was fractionally lower Thursday, dropping less than 1% to a session low of $1.58 a share, after the wireless video company reported receiving an order worth more than $1 million from French broadcaster AMP VISUAL TV. The order includes the company's Vislink HCAM 4K UHD systems, UltraReceivers and FocalPoint camera control equipment with delivery scheduled to begin tomorrow, Jan. 5.
